rektion: sich in etw. (Dat.) widerspiegeln; etw. (Akk.) widerspiegeln (fig.)
definition_de: ein Bild zurückwerfen wie ein Spiegel (Die Berge spiegeln sich im See wider.); übertragen: etwas zeigen oder ausdrücken (Die Entscheidung spiegelt unsere Werte wider.)
example_de: Am frühen Morgen spiegeln sich die schneebedeckten Berge im stillen See wider.
example_en: In the early morning the snow-capped mountains are reflected in the still lake.
user_example_de: Diese Entscheidungen spiegeln einfach unsere Einstellung zur Familie wider.
visual_idea: Literal collocation 'sich im See widerspiegeln': snowy mountains mirrored perfectly in a calm lake, symmetric around the waterline. The 'wider-' (back) is visible as the mirrored image; the figurative meaning builds on it and is in definition_de.
image_prompt: a perfectly still alpine lake at sunrise, snow-capped mountains and a dark pine forest mirrored exactly in the glassy water, the shoreline running across the middle of the frame so the scene is symmetrical, a small wooden rowing boat resting at the edge, soft pink and golden morning light
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: a perfectly still alpine lake at sunrise mirrors snow-capped mountains, a gentle breeze sends soft ripples across the water so the reflection trembles, then the surface calms and the mirror image becomes sharp again; static wide camera
